cards.title: THE PANTRY
cards.tagline: FIVE SHELVES. START WITH THE ONE THAT HIDES THE OLDEST BAG.
cards.objective: The pantry is where you find out the difference between what you buy and what you actually eat. This card is the map.
cards.start_here: PNZ-001 Dry Goods Shelves. Take one shelf completely off and onto the counter before you decide anything. A shelf sorted in place keeps its own history, and the bag that got pushed behind the cereal two years ago stays behind the cereal.
how_to_play: 1. Deal the five ZONE cards face up. Pick the one that is annoying you today, or take the one this card says to start at.
2. Lay out that zone's three FRICTION cards. Keep the ones that are true on your shelf. Put the rest back.
3. Turn a friction card over and pick the answer that is true. It names a ROOT CAUSE.
4. The root cause card names the ACTION cards that fix that cause. Pick the one that matches the time you actually have: fifteen or thirty minutes.
5. Do it standing up, with the card in your hand.
6. Read the victory condition out loud. If it is not true yet, you are not finished, and that is the whole scoring system.
7. Fill in the zone's STANDARD card with a pen and put it where the zone is.
8. Draw an EVENT card when an ordinary hard day happens, and see whether the standard held.
cards.players: 1 to 6. With more than one, deal the friction cards out and let each person keep the ones they believe. Disagreement is the useful part, not a problem to resolve before starting.
cards.six_s: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain
cards.safety_first: Do PNA-011 The Full Shelf Safety And Access Walk before any rebuild. It takes thirty minutes and covers every shelf's height, the stool, and every hard-to-reach spot.

cards.title: DRY GOODS SHELVES
cards.tagline: ONE BLOCK OF STAPLES. ONE LABEL EACH. READABLE FROM THE DOORWAY.
cards.objective: Holds the grains, pasta and cereals you actually cook from in a normal week.
callouts: Rice, pasta and oats standing together as one labeled block at chest height
Breakfast cereal boxes standing together as their own block
Every opened bag sealed inside a matching container
A handwritten date visible on each container's label
The fill level inside every container readable without lifting it
A two-step stool standing inside the pantry beneath the top shelf
cards.done_looks_like: Every opened bag is either sealed in a container with its opening date written on it, or gone. Pasta, rice and oats stand as one block, breakfast cereal as another, and you can read the level in every container from the doorway without lifting a thing.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: Reaching the top shelf from a kitchen chair or by standing on the bottom shelf edge. Keep a two-step stool inside the pantry, and if the stool is not there, that shelf is too high for anything you need weekly.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Glass grain jars stored above eye level. A full one is heavy, hands in a kitchen are wet, and glass on a hard floor puts the room out of use. Glass at chest height or lower, lidded plastic up top.

the_call.title: The bag you opened for one recipe
the_call.text: Half a kilo of buckwheat, the coarse polenta, the rice flour from the week you tried a new bread. You keep them because binning food feels wrong, and because you genuinely still intend to. Settle it with a rule: if it is open, and you cannot name the specific meal you will cook with it inside the next fourteen days, it leaves now. Unopened and in date, give it away while it is still worth having. Opened and more than a year old, it goes in the bin without further debate, because stale grain is not a saving you can ever spend.

cards.title: CANNED AND JARRED GOODS
cards.tagline: EVERY LABEL FACING OUT. NOTHING DENTED. THE OLDEST DATE UP FRONT.
cards.objective: Holds the cans and jars that turn an empty-fridge week into dinner.
callouts: Cans standing in rows on a stepped riser, every label facing outward
Tomatoes grouped in one row, beans in another, soup in a third
No dented seam or domed lid visible on any can
No jar standing hidden directly behind another jar
The oldest-dated can or jar standing at the front of its row
A clean, dry shelf edge with no sticky ring under any jar
cards.done_looks_like: Cans sit in rows on risers with every label facing you: tomatoes together, beans together, soup together. No dented seams, no domed lids, no jar hidden behind another jar, and the oldest date in each row standing at the front of it.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: A bulging or leaking can is a spoilage warning and no amount of cooking makes it safe. Bag it sealed, bin it, and wash the shelf underneath where it stood.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: A dense row of cans on a high shelf. One tin landing on a bare foot is a broken toe, and a glass sauce jar bursting on tile leaves splinters you find for weeks. Cans and glass belong below shoulder height.

the_call.title: The best-before you keep arguing with
the_call.text: The soup two years past its date, the chickpeas whose date has rubbed off, the fancy jar somebody gave you that you are saving for an occasion that has not arrived. Best-before is about quality rather than safety, so you have been keeping these on a technicality and never eating them. End the argument with one pass: anything past best-before goes into a meal in the next seven days or it goes out this week. Anything past a use-by date goes now. Anything dented on the seam, rusted, or domed goes now regardless of the date, and it does not go to the food bank either. If you would not open it tonight, you are not saving it, you are storing it.

cards.title: BAKING ZONE
cards.tagline: ONE LIFT-OUT BIN. LEAVENERS DATED. THE ALLERGEN SHELF STANDS APART.
cards.objective: Holds everything you need to start a bake without a trip to the shop first.
callouts: Flour, sugar and brown sugar standing in sealed one-handed containers
Baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and yeast together in one small dated box
A single lift-out bin holding cutters, cases and piping tips
A dedicated scoop and sealed container for nut flour standing apart at the end of the row
No loose sprinkles rolling free on the shelf
A washed scoop sitting inside the flour bin, not buried in the flour
cards.done_looks_like: Flour, sugar and brown sugar in sealed containers you can open one-handed. Baking powder, bicarbonate of soda and yeast together in one small box with their dates showing. Cutters, cases and piping tips in a single lift-out bin, and no loose sprinkles rolling around the shelf.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Cross-contact between nut flours and everything else on the shelf, plus small decorating pieces like silver balls and mini cutters sitting on a low shelf within a toddler's reach.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: Spilled flour or sugar on a hard kitchen floor is genuinely slick, and you will be walking a hot tray across it. Sweep the spill when it happens rather than when the bake is done.

the_call.title: The kit for the baker you meant to become
the_call.text: The piping set from the birthday you decorated once, the fondant, the third tart tin, the specialty flour from a month of enthusiastic bread. This is the hardest shelf in the pantry, because letting it go feels like admitting something about yourself. Here is the rule that settles it: keep the tools for what you have baked twice, and let go of the tools for what you have baked once. Twice means it is a thing you do. Once means it was a good afternoon, and the afternoon has already happened. Whatever survives that test earns its bin space. The rest goes to somebody who bakes this month, not into a box in the garage where you will meet it again in three years.

cards.title: SNACK AND LUNCH ZONE
cards.tagline: ONE BIN AT CHILD HEIGHT. ONE LINE TO FILL IT TO. EVERY LID MATCHED.
cards.objective: Holds what goes into a lunchbox, and what a child is allowed to take without asking.
callouts: One open bin standing at child height
A marked fill line visible inside the open bin
A higher shelf holding the snacks that need an adult's yes
Every reusable container with its own lid sitting on top of it
Lunch bags and ice packs standing next to the containers
No loose orphaned lid or lidless tub anywhere on the shelf
cards.done_looks_like: One open bin at child height holding only snacks you have already said yes to, and a higher shelf holding the ones that need an adult. Every reusable container has its own lid sitting on it, and the number of containers matches the number of lunches you genuinely pack.

safety_checks.question: Poison, choke, or strangle
safety_checks.text: Hard sweets, whole nuts and small round cheeses in an open bin a two-year-old can reach. The bin's contents are set by the youngest child in the house, not the oldest.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: A child climbing the shelving to reach the higher snack shelf. If it is worth climbing for, either move it out of the pantry entirely or fix the shelving unit to the wall.

the_call.title: Whether the answer is yours or the bin's
the_call.text: You are negotiating snacks several times a day, and every one of those is a fresh decision made while you are busy and being asked twice. The call is to move the decision off the moment and onto the shelf. Choose once, in daylight and not at four o'clock, exactly what a child may take without asking, and put precisely that in the open bin at their height. Everything else goes above eye line and requires you. Then hold the line: when the bin is empty at four o'clock, the answer is that the bin is empty, not that you will go and find something. That single refusal is what makes the bin real. Until you hold it, the bin is decoration and you are still the one being asked.

cards.title: BACKSTOCK AND BULK ZONE
cards.tagline: DATED ON ARRIVAL. A MAXIMUM ON THE EDGE. ONE ROW DEEP.
cards.objective: Holds the reserve that feeds the working shelves, and nothing else.
callouts: Sacks of rice standing at or below waist height
Cases of tinned tomatoes with the arrival month written on each one
Packs of kitchen roll stored up high, off the floor
A maximum number written on the shelf edge for each line
The count on the shelf sitting at or under its written maximum
Nothing stacked directly in front of anything else
cards.done_looks_like: Sacks of rice, cases of tinned tomatoes and packs of kitchen roll, each written on with the month it arrived, all standing at or below waist height. A maximum number written on the shelf edge for each line, and the count on the shelf sitting at or under it. Nothing stacked in front of anything else.

safety_checks.question: Fall, cut, or crush
safety_checks.text: Cases stacked above chest height, and a heavy rice sack lifted off the floor with a twist in your back. Stack low, and slide the sack out onto a step or a chair before you lift it properly.

safety_checks.question: Fall
safety_checks.text: A floor-stacked case left near the doorway of a dim pantry is a shin-height trip in the dark. Keep the floor inside the door clear and put a light where your hand reaches it before your foot does.

the_call.title: The warehouse pack that was not a saving
the_call.text: You bought the big one because the unit price was better, and some of it went stale, rancid, or simply boring before you reached the bottom. The honest question is not whether the price was good. It is whether you have ever finished one of these in time. So write down, for each item, the largest quantity you have genuinely used up before it turned, and make that number your maximum on the shelf edge. Until your count falls back below that number you do not buy the item again, whatever the shelf price is doing. Anything already over the line goes forward into meals this month or out to a food bank while it is still in date. A cupboard full of food you will not eat is not a store of value, it is money you have already spent.

cards.title: CLEAR THE SHELF AND SMELL-TEST IT
cards.objective: Bring down every bag and box on this shelf and smell-test every opened one, so nothing stale or forgotten survives on a technicality.
cards.why_it_matters: A bag with no date on it is impossible to judge honestly, so it just keeps not getting thrown out.
steps: Bring down every bag and box on this shelf, open anything already opened, and smell the flour and the oats: stale, webbed, or bought for a recipe you have not cooked in months leaves today.
For anything unopened and still in date but unlikely to get used, set it aside to give away rather than binning it.
Group what stays into two blocks on the shelf: rice, pasta and oats together, cereal together.
cards.victory_condition: Every opened bag is sealed in a labeled container or gone, and pasta, rice and oats stand together as one block.

art.subject: a pantry shelf mid-clear with two clean blocks forming, one of grain containers and one of cereal boxes, a bin bag sitting on the floor beside it
must_show: Every opened bag is sealed in a labeled container or gone, and pasta, rice and oats stand together as one block.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: LABEL EVERY CONTAINER AND MOVE THE GLASS DOWN
cards.objective: Give every staple one container style with a written open date, and move any glass jar down to chest height or lower.
cards.why_it_matters: A missing label makes every container's age a guess, and a glass jar above eye level is a real fall and cut risk beside wet hands.
steps: Decant each staple into one container style, and write the item and today's date on the label the moment it is opened.
Move every glass jar down to chest height or lower, and put lidded plastic containers up top instead.
Keep a two-step stool inside the pantry for anything that still sits on the top shelf.
cards.victory_condition: Every staple sits in a labeled container with its opening date on it, and no glass container sits above eye level.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a hand writing today's date on a labeled pantry container at chest height, a glass jar visible lower down on the shelf than a set of plastic containers above it

art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: PULL EVERY DENTED OR DOMED CAN
cards.objective: Take every can and jar off the shelf, check each one for damage or a bad date, and remove anything spoiled without debate.
cards.why_it_matters: A dented seam or a domed lid is a spoilage warning, not a judgment call, and it does not get tasted or given away.
steps: Take every can and jar off the shelf, turn each one to find the date, and put anything dented, rusted, bulging or domed straight into the bin rather than back on the shelf.
Bag anything spoiled sealed before it goes in the bin, and wipe the shelf underneath where it stood.
Set every surviving can and jar back with its label facing out.
cards.victory_condition: No dented, rusted, domed or bulging can or jar remains on the shelf, and every label faces out.

art.subject: a hand pulling a dented can off a pantry shelf and setting it apart from a row of undamaged, label-out cans
must_show: No dented, rusted, domed or bulging can or jar remains on the shelf, and every label faces out.
art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: ROW BY MEAL, LABEL EACH ROW, RISER UP
cards.objective: Rearrange cans and jars into rows by meal rather than by size, label each row, and put the back row up on a riser.
cards.why_it_matters: Four jars of the same sauce is what happens when nobody can see what is already on the shelf before buying another.
steps: Group cans and jars by meal: tomatoes, coconut milk and stock together, beans and tuna together, tall jars behind short cans.
Set the back row up on a riser so it sits visibly above the front row.
Label each row with its category so a gap reads as a shopping list from the doorway.
cards.victory_condition: Every row holds one category, is labeled, and the back row sits visibly above the front row on a riser.
cards.source: hand authored, steps grounded in the Manual passes

art.subject: a pantry shelf with cans arranged in labeled rows by meal, a riser lifting the back row visibly above the front row

art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: TEST EVERY LEAVENER, TOSS WHAT'S DEAD
cards.objective: Test every leavener rather than guessing, and remove anything dead along with hardened brown sugar or greyed cocoa.
cards.why_it_matters: A cake that will not rise on the day is the only way most households ever find out a leavener died months ago.
steps: Test every leavener rather than guessing: a spoon of baking powder in hot water should fizz hard, and yeast in warm sugared water should foam. The dead ones go, along with any hardened brown sugar or greyed cocoa.
Write today's date on the lid of anything that survives, including anything freshly opened.
cards.victory_condition: Every leavener in the bin has been tested this week, and nothing dead or expired remains.

art.subject: a spoon of baking powder fizzing in a glass of hot water on a pantry counter, a dated tin standing ready beside it

art.accept_test: The picture shows the finished state the victory condition describes, not the work in progress and not a person doing it.

cards.title: GIVE THE ALLERGEN SHELF ITS OWN SCOOP AND SPOT
cards.objective: Move nut flours and sesame to the end of the row with their own sealed container and their own scoop, never shared.
cards.why_it_matters: One shared scoop carries a trace of an allergen straight into a birthday cake, and nobody notices until somebody reacts.
steps: Move every nut flour and sesame product to the end of the row, away from where a hand grabs by habit.
Seal each one in its own container with its own scoop kept inside it, never shared with the rest of the shelf.
Label the container clearly so anyone baking in a hurry sees the warning before the scoop.
cards.victory_condition: Every allergen container stands at the end of the row, sealed, labeled, with its own dedicated scoop inside it.

steps: Match every lid to a container and bin the orphans in both directions, the lidless tubs and the lids for tubs that died. Pull any snack boxes with only a couple of bars rattling around and combine them.
Flatten and recycle the empty cartons.

the snacks you are choosing to allow

Refill it with only what you have said yes to, and mark a fill line inside the bin at the level it should sit at.
Move anything that still needs an adult up to the higher shelf.

steps: Open up the back of this zone and meet what you forgot you owned: any item you hold more than one genuine spare of moves forward into the working shelves this month or it leaves.
Write the arrival month on every remaining pack as it goes back.

cards.title: DATE EVERY CASE AND WRITE THE MAXIMUM
cards.objective: Write a maximum for each line on the shelf edge, and check every case is one row deep with nothing hidden behind it.
cards.why_it_matters: Undated bulk with no written limit is where a saving quietly expires out of sight, and a hidden case behind another one never gets pulled first.
steps: Pull every case forward to check nothing is stacked directly in front of another one of the same thing.
Write a maximum for each line on the shelf edge, based on the most you have genuinely used up before it turned.
Mark every case with its arrival month as it goes back, oldest at the front.

cards.title: THE FULL SHELF SAFETY AND ACCESS WALK
cards.objective: Walk every shelf checking what is stored above eye level, whether a stool is where it should be, and reaching the sticky spots nobody gets to on an ordinary pass.

steps: Check every shelf for glass or heavy items stored above eye level, and move them down to chest height or lower.

cards.title: THE WEEKLY GAP-AND-DATE PASS
cards.objective: Walk every shelf reading the gaps before the shopping list gets written, and name who is doing it this week.

Say out loud, or write down, whose turn it is to do this pass this week.

cards.title: THE MONTHLY OVER-BUY AUDIT
cards.objective: Once a month, check every written maximum and label against what is actually on the shelves, and correct any that have drifted.
cards.why_it_matters: A maximum written once and never revisited stops meaning anything the first time a genuinely good price tempts you past it.
inputs: this month's receipts if you kept them
steps: Compare the count on each backstock line against its written maximum, and note any line that has crept over.
For any line over its maximum, decide today whether the number was wrong or the buying was: correct the label, or commit to pausing that purchase.
Check that every open container still carries a legible date and relabel anything that has faded.
cards.victory_condition: Every backstock line sits at or under a maximum you checked this month, and every open container's date is legible.

Press a finger into the back corner where board meets upright and check for packed flour dust, then brush it clear.
Check the level in each container from the doorway, without lifting a single one, and note which one is close to empty.

cards.objective: One lift-out baking bin with a washed scoop, leaveners dated on the lid the day they are opened, and allergen flours sealed with a scoop of their own.
cards.trigger: When you set the oven to preheat, you check the leavener dates while it comes up to temperature.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Wash the baking bin's scoop in warm soapy water and dry it fully before it goes back into the flour.

cards.title: SNACK AND LUNCH ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: The open bin at child height holds only pre-approved snacks and is refilled to one marked level, and no container returns to the shelf without its lid on it.
cards.trigger: When the lunchboxes are emptied at the sink after school, the bin gets filled back to its line before the bags go on their hook.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Turn one lunch bag inside out and shake any crumbs into the bin before it goes back on its hook.
Wash a drink bottle's spout and screw thread where a sour film hides in the seam.
Wipe the bin's exterior and the shelf edge where sticky hands land most often.

art.subject: a pantry shelf with an open snack bin at child height filled to a marked line, a higher shelf above holding snacks that need an adult, reusable lunch containers each with its own lid sitting on top, and lunch bags with ice packs standing beside them, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: BACKSTOCK AND BULK ZONE STANDARD
cards.tagline: WRITE IT. SIGN IT. PUT IT WHERE IT HAPPENS.
cards.objective: Every pack carries its arrival month, every line has a maximum written on the shelf edge, and stock is always pulled from the front.
cards.trigger: When you get home from a big shop, you write the month on each pack with the marker that lives on that shelf, before anything gets put away.
cards.instruction: This is a write on card. Fill it in with a pen, in your own words if the printed sentence is not yours, and put it where the zone is. A standard nobody signed is a preference.
micro_quest: Lift the lowest case in one stack and feel its underside for damp before setting it back down.
Sweep the floor just inside the pantry doorway where a case at shin height hides in the dark.
Wipe one shelf edge label clean so its written maximum count stays readable from across the room.

art.subject: a pantry backstock area with sacks of rice and cases of tinned tomatoes standing at or below waist height, each case marked with its arrival month, light packs of kitchen roll stored higher up, a small dated sticker fixed to the shelf edge, and nothing stacked in front of anything else, photographed plainly with a generous area of empty calm surface across the lower half for the write on lines
must_show: the zone holding its standard
art.accept_test: The lower half of the frame must be visually quiet enough to print three blank lines over it and still read.

cards.title: THE MIDWEEK EMPTY-SHELF SCRAMBLE
cards.objective: You reach for pasta on a Tuesday night with no plan B, and the shelf has to answer honestly whether there's a full block of staples or a gap.
cards.held_if: A full, labeled block of rice, pasta and oats answers immediately, no hunting behind other boxes.
cards.if_it_failed: If you had to dig behind cereal boxes to find a bag that might still be good, the loading-behind rule slipped. Draw PNA-002.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.
cards.source: hand authored, not in the Manual

art.subject: a hand reaching confidently into a pantry shelf at dinner time and pulling out a labeled container of pasta from a tidy block of staples
must_show: You reach for pasta on a Tuesday night with no plan B, and the shelf has to answer honestly whether there's a full block of staples or a gap.
art.accept_test: The pressure has to be visible in the objects. No people's faces, so the load has to be shown by what is on the surfaces and, where unavoidable, by hands and feet alone.

cards.title: THE EMPTY-FRIDGE-WEEK DINNER
cards.objective: The fridge is bare and dinner has to come entirely from cans and jars tonight.
cards.held_if: Every can you reach for is legible, unspoiled and exactly where its row says it should be.
cards.if_it_failed: If you pulled a can and found it dented or hidden behind another, the spoilage or visibility check lapsed. Draw PNA-003.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.
cards.source: hand authored, not in the Manual

cards.title: THE UNPLANNED BIRTHDAY BAKE
cards.objective: Someone asks for a cake with two hours' notice and the baking bin has to answer for itself.
cards.held_if: The bin has a working scoop, dated leaveners that still test fresh, and vanilla exactly where it belongs.
cards.if_it_failed: If a leavener failed its fizz test or a tool was missing, the bin's own reset slipped. Draw PNA-005.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.

cards.title: THE MORNING NOBODY PACKED LUNCH THE NIGHT BEFORE
cards.objective: Lunches have to get packed in five rushed minutes before the bus, straight from whatever the bin already holds.
cards.held_if: The open bin is filled to its line with only pre-approved snacks, and every container has its matching lid.
cards.if_it_failed: If the bin was empty or a container had no lid, the evening refill did not happen. Draw PNA-007.
cards.instruction: Do not do anything to prepare. Live the day, then read the two lines below and be honest about which one you are.
cards.source: hand authored, not in the Manual

art.subject: a hand packing a lunchbox quickly from a well-stocked open snack bin at child height, every container already matched with its lid

art.accept_test: The pressure has to be visible in the objects. No people's faces, so the load has to be shown by what is on the surfaces and, where unavoidable, by hands and feet alone.

cards.title: THE SURPRISE BULK DELIVERY
cards.objective: A bulk order arrives unannounced and has to go somewhere in a backstock zone that is already at its stated limits.
cards.held_if: Every existing line sits at or under its written maximum, so the new delivery has an honest amount of room to go into.
cards.if_it_failed: If there was nowhere to put it without exceeding a written maximum, the pull-forward-and-stop-buying rule slipped. Draw PNA-009.
